summary: Proposed etymological description: borrowed Arabic mawǧūdīn, plural of the presence/existence participial adjective. This analysis is supplied in the reader record; no independent Arabic lexicon was consulted.
The Turoyo evidence is kətne tamo mawǧudin with plural people as state bearers. Their presence is asserted; no finding event, causer, or patient alternation is demonstrated.

Stem I is a provisional indexing convention based on the Arabic source form. The example uses Part. Pass. as a lexical-form description with detransitive=false; neither a finite Turoyo I paradigm nor productive Detransitive morphology is established.
The forms field explicitly reports unestablished Preterit/Infectum rather than generating them from the Arabic root. The accepted sense is limited to presence/availability, not finding.

Permitted lookup confirms that wǧd is absent. ʔǧd II means erfinden and is a separate formation; it must not absorb this occurrence. Search also finds mawǧūd in ftkr and qdm examples (and the same qdm wording under a twr idiom), supporting lexical presence usage without adding unassigned occurrence decisions.

Should the new wǧd record be published as a cross-reference for a loan adjective or as a verbal entry with provisional Part. Pass. filing? The requested proposal does not settle productive verbal status.
